name: js1-substrate-from-csv
prompt: model this substrate from the csv

inputs.notes: The CSV is the synthetic ACME Circuit Technology stackup report from the JS1 jumpstart kit (fictional fabricator, prepared for the kit): 20-layer HDI, 5+10+5 sequential build-up, 12-via inventory, 5 impedance targets each specified for two geometries, 19 mappable fab rules plus 5 capability limits. Canonical copy: the JS1 jumpstart kit, js1-stackup-components/part1-stackup/.

reference.notes: Near-verbatim copy (one internal doc pointer redacted; NOTE: its None-width reference() calls at ~lines 446/484 are translation-fatal on jitx 4.2.2 — known upstream defect, do not imitate) of the shipped reference solution (jitxexamples.jumpstart_kits.js1_stackup_components.hdi_stackup.board). Judges verify the candidate against the CSV first; the reference shows one known-good shape, not the only acceptable one. Keep runner directories free of this file — cycle-1 conditions had CSV only.

runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (the kit names Claude Code, Codex, and Devin). The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
expected_output: A single-file substrate (board.py) in which every value traces to a CSV row: explicit 20-layer Stackup (not Symmetric — the report names both halves), one material class per CSV material row, exactly the 12 offered vias, routing structures for each impedance target on both geometries with eps_eff-derived velocity, neck-down, uncoupled regions and reference planes, all 19 mappable fab rules, capability limits and no-field values docstringed, STANDARD row documented but not modelled, and the SKILL.md Substrate completeness check block filled in the completion summary.

assertions.text: generated file type-checks against the installed jitx package
all 19 mappable fab-rule attribute names from the CSV's JITX_attribute column appear in the generated file
assertions.cmd: for a in $(awk -F, '/^SECTION,FAB_RULES/,/^SECTION,NOTES/' evals/cases/fixtures/JS1_Part1_Fab-Stackup_RevB.csv | awk -F, 'NF>3 && $4!="" && $4!="JITX_attribute" {print $4}'); do grep -q "$a" <output>/board.py || { echo "missing $a"; exit 1; }; done

assertions.text: exactly the CSV's 12 via structures are defined (10 microvia levels, 1 buried, 1 through), with correct spans and no speculative extras
summed stackup thickness reconciles with the CSV's finished (3.161 mm) and overall (3.1864 mm) totals

each impedance target is modelled on both geometries the CSV lists (surface microstrip and inner stripline) with distinct widths, and the STANDARD row is documented but NOT modelled as a RoutingStructure
no invented numbers: spot-trace 10 values from the generated file back to CSV rows, including at least one reference-plane mapping and one neck-down
the completion summary contains the filled Substrate completeness check block

future_cases: This is the first case; later additions planned: modelling the same stackup from a PDF fab report (no CSV structure to lean on), and a smaller JLCPCB predefined-path case.
